description: Anomalix is a two-person team from São José do Rio Preto, Brazil. In statistics, an outlier is the data point that refuses to follow the pattern. That's us: two teenagers competing against the world. We turn NASA Earth data into clear, statistically honest answers about our changing climate - what is changing, where, by how much, and whether it's real signal or natural variation. We build tools that let anyone see the trend hiding inside the noise.
summary: Climate Detective answers one question for any place on Earth: is its climate really changing, or is it just noise? Type a city and the app pulls about 45 years of NASA POWER reanalysis data live, fits the trend, tests it for significance, and compares it with the global trend from NASA GISTEMP on the same years. For São José do Rio Preto, Brazil, the local warming is about 2.4 times the planet's rate.
details:
Is your city warming faster than the planet? Type any place on Earth and let NASA data, and an honest statistical test, answer.

Climate Detective is a web app that turns 45 years of NASA data into a clear verdict for any place on Earth. You type a city, pick a variable (air temperature at 2 m, precipitation, relative humidity or wind speed) and a period, and the app pulls the data live from NASA POWER (MERRA-2), fits the trend with a regression, tests it with a Mann-Kendall significance test, and compares it with the global trend from NASA GISTEMP v4 on the same years.

The verdict is honest by design: a warming claim is only shown when the statistics support it. Delhi, for example, comes back Inconclusive, because not significant does not mean no trend. A Brazil Grid view maps 710 real grid points across all 27 states and shows how each decade has warmed since the 1980s.

For São José do Rio Preto, Brazil, the app shows warming of +0.51 °C per decade against +0.21 °C globally, about 2.4 times the planet's rate, with p < 0.001.

Built with Next.js, live NASA APIs and real captures of the app in the demo video. Team: Anomalix.

AI tools assisted the coding. The video's music and motion graphics are AI generated, as marked in the video.
